recognition: No specific target study recognized. The supplied abstracts and bibliographic IDs were reviewed as provided; no full texts were independently consulted.
summary: The final relation search returned two abstracts (S_internal_domains_rna_condensates_S1-S2). S2 reports coexisting nucleolar subphases, composition-linked localization, and a pH gradient associated with acidic protein tracts co-condensed with nucleolar RNA. This supports a general precedent for multiphase organization in an RNA-associated condensate, not the proposed mechanism in engineered RNA droplets. S1 is a perspective identifying interfaces, active systems, and multiphases without a specific relation. The mechanism gap remains open. C05 executed successfully as an illustrative simulation: r=kf*max(x-xc,0), q*=qmax*r/(r+kc), q(t)=q*+(q0-q*)exp(-(r+kc)t); a carryover model with matched r gives identical trajectories. No fit or empirical causal test was performed. Evidence: S_internal_domains_rna_condensates_S1-S2, S_multiphase_wetting_domains_S1-S4, C05, C01-C04, E02, initial_measurements.json.

candidates.target: Explain emergence and persistence of B cavity q(t), deriving a discriminating prediction versus carryover-driven global phase change.
known_relations: A/B q(t) diverge after similar initial values; at 24 h A=0.00446 and B=0.08918 (initial_measurements.json).
C02 time fits are descriptive and model-sensitive; the 36/48 h commitment lacks preparation-level uncertainty.

S_multiphase_wetting_domains_S3 abstract review associates RNA sequence, structure, and modifications with RNA-mediated crowding/condensate behavior, without an internal-domain relation or quantitative law.

S_multiphase_wetting_domains_S1 abstract review describes protein condensate composition/miscibility responding to molecular or environmental changes; this is protein context and does not establish an RNA cavity mechanism.

S_multiphase_wetting_domains_S2 abstract discusses general molecular crowding without a partition-to-cavity relation; S4 discusses coacervate protocell compartmentalization/growth/division, not cavities inside transcribing RNA droplets.

C05 executed successfully with illustrative, unfitted parameter ranges. qss ranges across the grid were 0 at x=0; 0 to 0.499002 at x=0.1; 0 to 0.499750 at x=0.25; 0 to 0.499889 at x=0.5; and 0.033333 to 0.499947 at x=1. All were reported within the global [0,0.5] bound; the analytical expression bounds qss within each chosen qmax.
C05 carryover examples matched effective rates (0.02 h^-1 and 5 h^-1) and yielded identical q dynamics; this is model equivalence, not evidence favoring either driver.

S_internal_domains_rna_condensates_S2 reports coexisting nucleolar subphases, localization preferences related to protein IDRs and RNA/DNA-binding domains, and an in-vitro/cellular pH gradient associated with acidic protein tracts co-condensed with nucleolar RNA. Abstract-only and distinct from the engineered RNA system.
S_internal_domains_rna_condensates_S1 identifies interfaces, active systems and multiphases as research frontiers but supplies no specific quantitative mechanism.
hypotheses: NEW, system-specific provisional hypothesis (novelty not established): during transcription, a changing reference/variant RNA mixture plus selective partitioning can move local composition across a demixing threshold and nucleate an internal RNA-poor domain; interfacial cost and slow exchange may prolong it. Nucleolar literature makes multiphase organization in an RNA-associated condensate plausible, but does not demonstrate this bridge or its transfer to the engineered construct.

gaps.description: No matched time course links RNA proportions or phase composition to cavity nucleation and persistence in this system. Nucleolar subphase evidence is a biological analogue, not a causal relation for engineered RNA droplets; wetting, interface and exchange conditions remain unknown.

equations: Unclosed phenomenological model: dq/dt=kf*max(x-xc,0)*(qmax-q)-kc*q. It does not derive x(t), thermodynamics, or internal topology.
For fixed x and kc>0, r=kf*max(x-xc,0), q*=qmax*r/(r+kc), and q(t)=q*+(q0-q*)exp(-(r+kc)t). If x<=xc, r=0 and q(t)=q0*exp(-kc*t), with decay half-life ln(2)/kc.
Carryover alternative: dq/dt=kg*max(c-cc,0)*(qmax-q)-kc*q. If kg*max(c-cc,0)=kf*max(x-xc,0), trajectories are identical; q(t) alone cannot identify the driver.
For a measured phase species i, Ki=Ci,dense/Ci,dilute only when the dilute concentration is positive; no supported mapping from Ki to q.

parameters_ranges.kf: positive h^-1; unmeasured; C05 used illustrative 0.1-10 h^-1
parameters_ranges.kc: positive h^-1; unmeasured; C05 used illustrative 0.001-0.1 h^-1
parameters_ranges.x: [0,1]; C05 grid {0,0.1,0.25,0.5,1} is illustrative, not observed

candidates.observation_mapping: q maps only to the supplied mean per-object segmented empty-area fraction. It is not concentration, volume fraction, or ratio of total dark area to total filled area. x, c, and time-varying phase concentrations are unmeasured.
alternatives: Carryover or other reaction conditions drive a global phase-state change; the same mathematical form explains q(t).
Population turnover, field sampling, or segmentation changes mean q while individual cavity state is stable; tracking does not establish within-droplet cavity trajectories.
predictions: At matched carryover and total RNA, titrating measured RNA mixture fraction should shift q onset/steady state if composition is causal; fixed x above xc predicts q* increasing with x and below xc predicts decay toward zero.

Factorially vary composition and measured carryover. A pure composition mechanism predicts residual composition dependence under matched carryover; a pure carryover mechanism predicts response to carryover at fixed composition. Matching effective rates explains why observational q(t) alone cannot discriminate.
If q rises while x is constant, the specific changing-composition driver is weakened; after x falls below xc, this model predicts exponential relaxation with half-life ln(2)/kc.

evidence_conflicts: E02 is compatible with a mixture effect but is not a controlled dose-response and does not measure RNA composition over time.
C04 endpoint partitions and abstract literature do not explain internal geometry, nucleation, or persistence.
A/B are confounded by possible carryover; q is an image metric and tracking does not identify persistent within-droplet cavity state.
Nucleolar S2 supports coexisting subphases and composition-specific properties in a distinct RNA/protein system, but not cavities in engineered droplets or their cause.

dissent: C05 is valid as a conditional ODE calculation, but its parameter ranges are intentionally broad and the global-bound check is weaker than checking each row against its own qmax; the analytical bound resolves that mathematical point. It supplies no empirical mechanism evidence.

R2 accurately noted S1-S4 did not establish a cavity mechanism. The new S_internal_domains_rna_condensates_S2 result does establish a general multiphase analogue in an RNA-associated condensate, revising the broader claim that no relevant internal or multiphase relation was found. It does not close the system-specific causal gap.

final.question_and_reason: Does changing reference/variant RNA composition, under controlled carryover and total RNA, trigger an internal RNA-poor domain in transcribing four-arm RNA condensates? Current observations and abstracts cannot separate this from carryover-driven global phase change or population/measurement effects.
final.increment: S_internal_domains_rna_condensates_S2 adds a relevant analogue: coexisting nucleolar subphases and composition-linked physicochemical properties occur in an RNA-associated biological condensate. It does not establish this engineered-droplet mechanism; novelty remains unverified.
final.new_hypotheses: Provisional system-specific hypothesis: changing RNA composition with selective partitioning crosses a demixing threshold, nucleates an internal dilute domain, and interfacial cost or slow exchange may sustain it. This is not established or verified as novel.
final.actual_derivation_or_computation: C05 executed (returncode 0, stderr empty) with qmax={0.1,0.5}, xc={0.05,0.5}, kf={0.1,10} h^-1, kc={0.001,0.1} h^-1, x={0,0.1,0.25,0.5,1}. It is illustrative and unfitted. For fixed x, r=kf*max(x-xc,0), q*=qmax*r/(r+kc), q(t)=q*+(q0-q*)exp(-(r+kc)t). Across the grid q* ranged [0,0] at x=0, [0,0.499002] at 0.1, [0,0.499750] at 0.25, [0,0.499889] at 0.5, and [0.033333,0.499947] at 1. Matched carryover examples reproduced rates 0.02 and 5 h^-1, so this model cannot identify cause from q(t). No fit to observations or physical computation was performed.
final.discriminating_prediction: Measure RNA mixture and carryover directly, then factorially perturb composition and carryover while holding total RNA and remaining conditions matched. Composition causality predicts residual composition-dependent onset/steady q at matched carryover; pure carryover predicts response to carryover at fixed composition. Longitudinal RNA/phase and 3D cavity measurements test whether composition changes precede nucleation and whether cavities persist after composition falls below threshold.
final.evidence_support_conflict_untested: Support: A/B q divergence by 24 h; E02 length-fraction endpoint differences; S2 nucleolar coexisting subphases/pH organization as abstract-only analogue; C05 conditional dynamics. Limits: E02 is not a mixture titration; C04 endpoints do not map to q; DNA reads do not establish RNA abundance; A/B may differ in carryover; q is segmented area, and C03 lacks persistent cavity trajectories. Untested: RNA species over time, cavity 3D identity, interfaces, exchange and matched composition/carryover causality.
final.decision: Complete the literature-review task but leave the mechanism gap open. The mixture-threshold model is a useful conditional representation, not a validated explanation.
final.dissent: S2 revises the earlier broad statement that literature supplied no relevant internal/multiphase relation, but does not support the target-specific causal chain. C05 is illustrative, broad-ranged and has no empirical identifying power; its code checked a global qmax bound, while the formula supplies the per-case bound.
final.next_experiment: Matched-total-RNA factorial titration of measured reference/variant RNA composition and directly measured carryover, with serial RNA abundance/phase-partition measurements and longitudinal 3D cavity tracking. No such experiment was performed in this run.
final.limitations: Literature support is abstract-only. C05 parameters are illustrative and unfitted; its ODE omits spatial geometry and thermodynamics. q is image-derived area, not concentration or phase volume; replication is preparation-limited; no empirical intervention distinguishes composition from carryover.
